answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicates, like a raven leaving the same feather in two nests. Verification then checks work history across a karst of independent attestors rather than trusting a single claim, so one actor must pay and perform repeatedly for every fake. A short public sonnet of commitments — what the agent will do, how it can be checked, and what it forfeits — makes cheap copies easy to spot and expensive to maintain.
